title: api: unify rate-limit semantics, idempotency and Retry-After for streaming/openai-compat
author: Morgan Chen
description: Motivation: inconsistent rate-limit behavior across the API surface (classic request/response, streaming, and the OpenAI compatibility layer) caused confusing client behavior during peaks and made client-side retry logic brittle. This PR unifies semantics for 429 responses and Retry-After propagation, formalizes idempotency keys for streaming endpoints, and standardizes OpenAI-compat error bodies so client SDKs can reliably implement backoff and resume logic. Summary of changes: 1) Gateway layer now forwards upstream Retry-After headers and synthesizes Retry-After for internal throttles; 2) All endpoints (including /v1/chat/stream, /v1/responses and OpenAI-compat endpoints) return a consistent 429 body: {"error": {"type": "rate_limit_error", "message": "...", "code": "rate_limit"}} and a Retry-After header (seconds). This matches OpenAI compatibility expectations; we still include our internal x-rw-rl-policy header for debugging but it is optional for clients; 3) Introduced streaming idempotency: clients may provide x-idempotency-key for streaming requests. When provided, the gateway creates an idempotency record (id + status) in the idempotency store and ensures retries with the same key are deduplicated. For streaming requests that partially completed prior to a throttle or transient failure we record last-committed event offset and will either resume (when requested and supported by client) or return an explicit 409 with a consistent operation status payload so clients can decide to resume or issue a new request; 4) OpenAI-compat layer: map internal transient errors to OpenAI-compatible error types and codes (rate_limit_error, server_error, invalid_request_error) and include the Retry-After header where applicable; 5) SDK compatibility: python/typescript SDKs updated to prefer Retry-After header behavior and to surface idempotency guidance in docstrings; 6) Tests and observability: added unit + integration tests for Retry-After propagation, idempotency key handling for streaming, and end-to-end flaky-streaming regression tests; added metrics (api.rate_limit.propagated, idempotency.store.hits/misses, streaming.resume.attempts) and dashboards updated. Backwards compatibility: non-idempotent clients are unaffected; endpoints without x-idempotency-key keep existing behavior. For OpenAI-compat consumers the 429 body shape is backwards compatible (we preserve message and include code). Implementation notes: - Gateway changes in redwood/gateway/proxy (propagate Retry-After, synthesize when our rate limiter triggers). - New idempotency service at redwood/runtime/idempotency with a small TTL-backed store (redis-backed) recording keys -> {status, last_offset, response_ref}. - Streaming runtime updates to checkpoint offsets to idempotency records on commit events. - SDK updates in redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript to expose idempotency-key parameter and to surface Retry-After via SDK exceptions. Testing / rollout: staged rollout behind feature flag enable_streaming_idempotency; ramped traffic in Dedicated Canary and Hosted with a 24-hour observation window; alerts configured for unexpected increases in idempotency-store size or resume failure rate. Performance: microbenchmark shows ~2% median tail increase in gateway latency under heavy idempotency key write load; we added batching to idempotency writes and tuned TTLs to limit overhead. Known limitations / future work: resume semantics currently require client participation (explicit resume request) for complex multi-tool invocations; we plan to evaluate automatic resume for single-tool streams in follow-ups. This PR also includes several hotfixes for a race between streaming cancellation and rate limit enforcement reported in incident INT-2214. See commits and review discussion for details.

release_notes: Standardizes 429/RateLimit responses and exposes Retry-After header across streaming and non-streaming endpoints.
Adds optional x-idempotency-key support for streaming endpoints with deduplication and resume guidance.
OpenAI-compat layer now returns consistent error types/codes for transient rate limits and includes Retry-After.
SDKs updated to surface Retry-After and idempotency-key usage.
